sources.title: Baidu Java backend interview note exact permutations prompt
Fresh backtracking versus independent lexicographic next-permutation validation

claims.text: The source asks only to hand-write full permutations; language, duplicate-value semantics, ordering, empty and null behavior are not preserved source constraints.
The candidate explicitly defines distinct integer values, one empty permutation for empty input and null rejection, leaving unique duplicate-value permutations as a separately clarified variant.
For n=0..8 fixed inputs and 120 randomized distinct arrays, the implementation has n! unique results exactly equal to an independent lexicographic next-permutation result set.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed-n=0..8 randomized=120 oracle=lexicographic-next-permutation distinct-input=true count-factorial=true no-duplicates=true empty-one=true null-rejected=true
checks: all distinct-input sizes n=0..8 have factorial result count
candidate result set matches an independent lexicographic next-permutation oracle
120 deterministic randomized distinct arrays with shuffled input order match the oracle
candidate emits no duplicate rows under the declared distinct-input contract
empty array returns exactly one empty permutation
null input is rejected by the declared API contract

boundary_tests.expected: exactly n! unique rows equal to independent lexicographic enumeration
set equality with independent next-permutation oracle regardless of input traversal order

findings: The repository source recoverably asks only to hand-write a full-permutation algorithm; it does not preserve language, input representation, duplicate-value semantics, output ordering, empty-input behavior, or null behavior.

The candidate explicitly narrows the executable contract to distinct integer inputs, one empty permutation for an empty array, and null rejection, while presenting duplicate-value deduplication only as a separately clarified variant.
The used-position plus mutable-path backtracking invariant generates every distinct-input permutation exactly once and snapshots the path at leaves.
Fresh validation checks all sizes n=0..8 and 120 deterministic randomized distinct arrays against an independent lexicographic next-permutation enumerator.
Factorial result counts, result-set equality, no duplicate rows, empty-input behavior, and null rejection all pass.
The O(n * n!) output-cost explanation and O(n) working-state bound are consistent with explicit materialization of all length-n results.
No unrelated generated-baseline material or fabricated project experience remains.
